title: Rivonia Trial
summary: In a Pretoria trial that lasted about eight months, leaders of the anti-apartheid movement faced sabotage charges after arrests at Liliesleaf Farm in Rivonia. On 12 June 1964 Nelson Mandela and seven others were sentenced to life imprisonment, not the death penalty they had expected, and the Black prisoners were flown to Robben Island.

uncertainty.note: The opened pages do not give the trial start date, only that it lasted eight months (UCT) or eight-and-a-half months (Nelson Mandela Foundation); start year 1963 is inferred. Convictions were on 11 June and sentencing on 12 June 1964.

where.modern_name: Palace of Justice, Pretoria, South Africa
where.historical_name: Palace of Justice, Pretoria, South Africa (arrests at Liliesleaf Farm, Rivonia, Johannesburg)

importance.justification: The trial imprisoned the core ANC leadership for decades and made Mandela an international symbol of resistance to apartheid.

related.because: The sabotage prosecution targeted opponents of the apartheid system built after 1948.

sources.title: Nelson Mandela sentenced to life imprisonment 44 years ago

reviewer_note: Least sure of the start date (inferred from trial length) and the count of accused: UCT says eleven accused with all but two convicted; the Foundation names eight sentenced and Rusty Bernstein acquitted on 11 June.
